comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C37-C40 regarding preparation timing constraints from network timescales. Both evaluations find these claims supported by the data, with peer reviewers noting the manuscript's useful discussion of preparation timing.

Perfect agreement on claims C44-C50, C52 regarding 2D network analyses. Both evaluations support these findings, with peer reviewers praising the mathematically tractable analyses and detailed dissection of low-dimensional networks.

Perfect agreement on claims C21, C53-C56 regarding the theoretical framework linking network properties to preparation. Both evaluations support the mechanistic explanation, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming the connection between network structure and optimal preparation.

Perfect agreement on claim C10 demonstrating that movement can be produced without preparatory inputs. Both evaluations support this as valid motivation for the study, with peer reviewers confirming this establishes the novelty of asking why preparation occurs.

Divergent evaluations on claim C70 (main conclusion). OpenEval finds it well-supported by comprehensive modeling results. Peer reviewers acknowledge valuable theoretical insight but express uncertainty due to limitations in accounting for other objectives, applicability to feedback-driven movements, and questions about generalizability.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C20, C27-C30, C35-C36 regarding core findings from optimal control modeling. Both evaluations support these claims, with all peer reviewers explicitly affirming that preparation emerges naturally under input constraints.

Divergent evaluations on claims C22, C63-C69 regarding sequential reach modeling. OpenEval finds claims supported with clear reproduction of experimental findings. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting consistency with some observations but identifying significant discrepancies in input shape, timing, and correlation patterns compared to actual data.

Divergent evaluations on claims C18-C19, C75-C77 regarding methodological framework. OpenEval finds the approach clearly documented and appropriate. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, acknowledging theoretical value but raising concerns about iLQR's limited ability to leverage nonlinearities, biological implausibility, and potential confounding of objectives with optimization procedures.

Agreement on claims C33-C34 regarding cost reduction mechanism. OpenEval supports these as part of broader modeling findings. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this mechanism, noting that preparation reduces input costs when networks have strong dynamics.

Both address claim C62 (experimental finding from Zimnik and Churchland). OpenEval finds it accurately summarizes the cited study. Peer reviewers note consistency with some observations but identify discrepancies in the model's reproduction of these findings.
OpenEval finds claims C1-C3, C8-C9 (established findings from prior work) well-supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval finds claims C6-C7, C11-C17 (theoretical frameworks and prior modeling approaches) accurately summarize established work with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval finds claim C43 (E-I network dynamics) accurately describes established knowledge with appropriate citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background claim.
OpenEval finds claims C71-C73 (source of experimental data) are factual statements with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
